nodes.label: Scoring Weight Environment Configuration
nodes.rationale: SCORING_SKILL_WEIGHT 0.40, EXPERIENCE 0.20, EDUCATION 0.10, SEMANTIC 0.30 plus MIN_SKILL_MATCH_THRESHOLD 0.3 and versioned PROMPT_VERSION/SCORING_VERSION are injected as env vars, so scoring can be retuned per environment and past scores remain attributable to a version.

nodes.label: AI Service Python Dependencies
nodes.rationale: fastapi/uvicorn, inngest pinned >=0.5.19,<0.6.0 to avoid breaking SDK changes, qdrant-client, llama-index + readers-file, pydantic/pydantic-settings, openai, httpx, tenacity for retries, structlog for structured logs and numpy. Note FlagEmbedding (local BGE-M3) is referenced in the docs but absent here, so EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=local needs an extra install.

nodes.label: Structured Candidate Profile Extraction
nodes.rationale: GPT-4o-mini output is validated with Pydantic so a malformed or hallucinated profile fails fast instead of propagating into scoring.

nodes.label: Deterministic Candidate Ranking
nodes.rationale: Ranking reuses already-stored MatchScores sorted by overall_score descending and only then attaches RAG explanations, so ordering never depends on LLM output.

nodes.label: Inngest Workflow Definitions
nodes.rationale: candidate/ingest-resume, candidate/score-job, candidate/rag-summary and job/rank-candidates run every long operation asynchronously with retries and idempotency, so a failed LLM or embedding step is retried rather than surfaced to the HTTP caller.

nodes.label: Evidence-Based RAG Summary with Reranking
nodes.rationale: Retrieve top 20 chunks, rerank with BGE-reranker-v2-m3 to top 10, keep the top 5 as evidence, then have GPT-4o-mini write a grounded summary. Two-stage retrieve-then-rerank raises precision while keeping the LLM context small, and attaching evidence chunks makes the explanation checkable.

nodes.label: Resume Ingestion (PDF to Qdrant)
nodes.rationale: LlamaIndex PDFReader extracts text, SentenceSplitter chunks at 1000 with 200 overlap so semantic context spans chunk boundaries, GPT-4o-mini extracts the profile, BGE-M3 embeds each chunk and chunks land in Qdrant with metadata.

nodes.label: Deterministic Candidate-Job Scoring Algorithm
nodes.rationale: overall = skill*0.40 + experience*0.20 + education*0.10 + semantic*0.30, with required skills at 70% and preferred at 30%, graded experience bands (>=required 100%, within 2y 90%, within 5y 80%, else proportional), graded education bands (100/70/40/10) and semantic as mean cosine similarity of the top 10 chunks. Deterministic rather than LLM-judged so the same inputs always yield the same score and rankings are auditable.

nodes.label: Candidate Ranking Flow
nodes.rationale: Ranking consumes previously stored match scores rather than rescoring, sorts by overall score, attaches RAG summaries for top candidates and POSTs to /api/ai/rankings/{jobId}.

nodes.label: Planned RAG Summary Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Context is built as Job Requirements + Candidate Profile before prompting, so the LLM output (fit assessment, matching skills, experience highlights, gaps, hiring recommendation) is grounded in retrieved text rather than free-form generation.

nodes.label: Planned Ranked Candidates Endpoint
nodes.rationale: GET /api/jobs/{jobId}/candidates/ranked returns a page sorted by aiMatchScore DESC with a minScore filter; Python batch-scores and caches embeddings so repeat ranking does not re-embed.

nodes.label: AI Service Monitoring & Observability
nodes.rationale: Structured JSON logging via structlog plus a health endpoint reporting dependency status, with the Inngest and Qdrant dashboards covering workflow and vector-store metrics instead of a bespoke metrics stack.

nodes.label: resume_chunks Qdrant Collection Schema
nodes.rationale: 1024-dim cosine vectors keyed by candidate_id, resume_id, nullable job_id, chunk_id, section, source_pdf, text, metadata and created_at; the keyword fields exist so retrieval can be filtered to one candidate before similarity search.

nodes.label: Resume Embedding & Candidate AI Field Migrations
nodes.norm_label: resume embedding & candidate ai field migrations
nodes.rationale: V3 adds resumes.resume_embedding vector(768) with an ivfflat cosine index for approximate nearest-neighbour search; V4 adds ai_match_score, matching_skills/potential_gaps as JSONB, ai_summary and ai_analyzed_at so AI output is persisted alongside the candidate rather than recomputed.

nodes.label: Model Configuration (BGE-M3, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen3)
nodes.rationale: Qwen3-Embedding-8B is kept as a reference/foundation model while BGE-M3 does the actual embedding work and GPT-4o-mini handles extraction, summaries and explanations - a cheap small LLM is sufficient because scoring itself is deterministic.

nodes.label: Stateless AI Service Design
nodes.rationale: 'The AI service does not store candidate, job, or user data. It only processes AI tasks.' It reads profiles and job descriptions from Spring Boot and POSTs MatchScore, RAGSummary and RankingResult back, so Spring Boot stays the single system of record and tenancy/auth never has to be duplicated in Python.

nodes.label: ai_resume_postgres container (pgvector/pg16)
nodes.rationale: Uses the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image so the vector extension is available without a custom build, publishes 5433:5432 to avoid clashing with a host PostgreSQL, and keeps postgres_data as a named volume with restart: unless-stopped.

nodes.label: Company Verification Flow (planned)
nodes.rationale: Admin email verification, email link, phone OTP, submitted verification details, then Platform Admin review before companyVerified=true. The frontend must never set companyVerified, so trust is only ever granted by the platform side.

nodes.label: CustomUserDetails SecurityContext Chain
nodes.rationale: CustomUserDetails wraps the User entity so the current company is reachable as customUserDetails.getUser().getCompany().getId(); this is the designated substitute for accepting companyId from a client request.

nodes.label: User Roles (PLATFORM_ADMIN, ADMIN, RECRUITER)
nodes.rationale: PLATFORM_ADMIN verifies companies at platform level and is only partially implemented; ADMIN and RECRUITER both belong to exactly one company. ADMIN sees company-wide data, RECRUITER only its permitted recruitment data, so role alone determines authorization scope.

nodes.label: Admin to Recruiter Management
nodes.rationale: Recruiter company is derived from the authenticated admin's SecurityContext instead of the request body so a client cannot inject another company's id. Role is forced to RECRUITER by the backend. Admin cannot delete self, preventing a company from losing its only administrator.

nodes.label: Company Registration & Verification Module
nodes.rationale: POST /api/company/register creates Company + first ADMIN atomically in one transaction so a half-registered company can never exist; GST uniqueness is validated to prevent duplicate company registration. Company starts companyVerified=false because verification is a platform-controlled process, never client-settable.

nodes.label: Recruiter Credential Email Service
nodes.rationale: Company name in the credential email is pulled from the admin's security context rather than static config so multi-tenant emails are correct. The app is deliberately allowed to start without mail configuration so local development is not blocked by missing SMTP credentials.

nodes.label: Backend Entity Model and Relationships
nodes.rationale: Company 1->N User, Company 1->N Job, Job 1->N Candidate, Candidate 1->1 Resume gives every company-owned entity a clear ownership path back to Company, which is what makes service-level company isolation checkable.

nodes.label: Job Management (Recruiter & Admin Endpoints)
nodes.rationale: Endpoints are split into /api/recruiter/jobs and /api/admin/jobs rather than one polymorphic route, so the authorization scope is explicit per path: recruiters are filtered to createdBy = current user and must be the creator to mutate, admins may act on any job within their own company.

nodes.label: Role-Based Navigation & Protected Routes
nodes.rationale: Navigation branches on ADMIN / RECRUITER / PLATFORM_ADMIN and routes are auth-guarded, but this is presentation only; the project rules state authorization must still be enforced in the backend because frontend filtering can be bypassed.

nodes.label: Company Isolation Rules
nodes.rationale: Query authorization is enforced at the service/repository level and never by frontend filtering, since a filtered UI still issues a reachable API call. Every company-owned entity needs a clear ownership path for this to be enforceable.

nodes.label: Controller to Service to Repository Architecture
nodes.norm_label: controller to service to repository architecture
nodes.rationale: Business logic stays in Services and database access stays in Repositories so authorization and company-isolation checks live in exactly one layer and cannot be bypassed by a controller reaching into a repository directly.

nodes.label: Never Trust Client-Provided Ownership Fields
nodes.rationale: companyId, role, createdBy and verification flags are never read from the request because a client could escalate privilege or cross tenants by setting them; ownership must come from the authenticated user instead.

nodes.label: Repository Method Naming Must Match Entity Properties
nodes.norm_label: repository method naming must match entity properties
nodes.rationale: Spring Data derives queries from method names, so existsByEmail is valid only if the entity has an email property; existsByCompanyEmail fails at context startup unless companyEmail genuinely exists. Uniqueness is additionally enforced at the database level, with service-level duplicate checks kept only for friendly error messages.

nodes.label: Company Isolation Security Requirement
nodes.rationale: Declared the critical security requirement: every User and Job belongs to a Company, a recruiter must never reach another company's data, ownership is always enforced by the backend, and companyId from the frontend is never trusted.

nodes.label: Company Identity & Uniqueness Criteria
nodes.rationale: Registration number is the intended duplicate-company identity criterion, with GST number optionally unique; company email and phone are deliberately NOT identity criteria because multiple legitimate companies can share or change contact details.

nodes.label: ai-service container
nodes.rationale: Reaches the Java backend at http://host.docker.internal:8080 because the backend runs on the host rather than inside this compose network, and waits on qdrant service_healthy before starting so the first ingest cannot fail on a cold vector store.

nodes.label: inngest dev container
nodes.rationale: Runs `inngest dev -u http://ai-service:8000/api/inngest`, so the dev server discovers the FastAPI app's Inngest handler by its in-network service name.

nodes.label: qdrant container
nodes.rationale: Healthcheck probes the TCP port directly via /dev/tcp rather than an HTTP path, with a 20s start_period, and persists to the qdrant_data volume so embeddings survive container recreation.

nodes.label: Java Job Embedding Service
nodes.rationale: Job embeddings are generated in Java via Spring AI / Ollama and stored as float[] jdEmbedding in the Job entity (pgvector), keeping the job-side vector co-located with relational job data instead of pushing it to the external vector store.

nodes.label: FastAPI AI Service (README view)
nodes.rationale: FastAPI + Python 3.12 + LlamaIndex + Inngest on port 8000, doing resume ingestion, GPT-4o-mini profile extraction, deterministic scoring (40/20/10/30), RAG summaries with reranked evidence, ranking with explanations and async workflows.

nodes.label: Full-Stack Architecture Overview
nodes.rationale: Frontend (5173) -> Spring Boot (8080) -> FastAPI AI service (8000), with PostgreSQL+pgvector (5433) behind the backend and Qdrant (6333) plus Inngest (8288) behind the AI service, so relational and vector stores are owned by different services.

nodes.label: Spring Boot Backend Service
nodes.rationale: Documented here as Spring Boot 3.4 on Java 21 with Spring Security, JWT (jjwt 0.12.7), MapStruct 1.6.3, Lombok and Spring AI (Ollama), serving REST at http://localhost:8080/api.

nodes.label: Service Environment Variable Reference
nodes.rationale: Backend requires JWT_SECRET (min 32 chars), mail and datasource settings plus AI_SERVICE_URL; the AI service requires OPENAI_API_KEY and SPRING_BOOT_BASE_URL while EMBEDDING_PROVIDER and RERANKER_PROVIDER default to local so the stack runs without paid embedding calls.

nodes.label: React + Vite Frontend Service
nodes.rationale: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite 5 + TailwindCSS 3.4 with React Router 6, React Hook Form + Zod, Recharts, Lucide and date-fns, served on port 5173.

nodes.label: Inngest Async Workflow Engine
nodes.rationale: Chosen for async job processing with retries on port 8288, so long-running LLM and embedding work survives failures instead of being lost in a request-scoped thread.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector
nodes.rationale: Holds relational data plus vector embeddings on port 5433; the non-default port avoids collision with a locally installed PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: Qdrant Vector Database
nodes.rationale: Qdrant v1.9 on 6333 stores resume chunk embeddings (BGE-M3, 1024-dim), keeping high-volume chunk vectors out of the transactional database.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting Runbook
nodes.rationale: Documents the recurring failure modes: database connection refused, Qdrant unreachable, BGE-M3 failing to load (fall back to EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai), Inngest not triggering because signing keys differ between services, and frontend API failures from VITE_API_BASE_URL or CORS.

nodes.label: Inngest Event Relay via AI Service
nodes.norm_label: inngest event relay via ai service
nodes.rationale: The Java backend sends events over REST to the AI service, which then forwards them to Inngest, because no Java Inngest SDK is available; the documented alternative is calling the Inngest REST API directly from Java.

nodes.label: Candidate Scoring Flow
nodes.rationale: Java fetches the Job, builds a JobDescription DTO and emits ScoreJobEvent; Python embeds the JD, pulls candidate chunks from Qdrant, scores skills/experience/education/semantic and POSTs the result back to /api/ai/match-scores.

nodes.label: RAG Summary Flow
nodes.rationale: Java emits RAGSummaryEvent only; all retrieval, reranking and generation happen in Python and the grounded summary is POSTed back to /api/ai/rag-summaries.

nodes.label: AICallbackController (/api/ai/* callbacks)
nodes.rationale: Receives match-scores, rag-summaries, rankings/{jobId} and candidate-profile pushed back by the Python service, which is what lets the AI service stay stateless. Flagged as an open risk: these callback routes are not yet secured by API key or JWT.

nodes.label: AI Event & Result DTO Model (dto/ai)
nodes.rationale: IngestResumeEvent, ScoreJobEvent, RAGSummaryEvent and RankCandidatesEvent on the outbound side and JobDescription, JobRequirement, MatchScore, RAGSummary, EvidenceChunk, RankedCandidate and RankingResult on the inbound side form the typed contract shared with the Python Pydantic schemas.

nodes.label: AIServiceClient (Java WebClient integration)
nodes.rationale: Implemented as an interface plus a WebClient implementation configured in AIServiceConfig, pointing at ai-service.base-url with a 300000ms timeout because AI workflows are long-running; spring-boot-starter-webflux was added to pom.xml for this.

nodes.label: CandidateServiceImplementation (upload orchestration)
nodes.rationale: Orchestrates upload -> persist Candidate+Resume to PostgreSQL -> store the PDF -> emit IngestResumeEvent to the AI service, so the HTTP upload returns immediately and the heavy work happens in Inngest.

nodes.label: Candidate Profile Page with AI Analysis Tab
nodes.norm_label: candidate profile page with ai analysis tab

nodes.label: FileStorageService (local filesystem)
nodes.rationale: Local filesystem implementation behind an interface at app.file.storage.path=./uploads; the interface exists so S3/MinIO can replace it for production, which is still an open TODO.

nodes.label: Integration Known Issues & TODOs
nodes.rationale: Java currently relays Inngest events through the AI service because there is no Java Inngest SDK; file storage is local-only; the extracted candidate profile is not yet synced back to the Candidate entity; workflow triggers are fire-and-forget with no status endpoint for UI feedback; /api/ai/* callbacks are unauthenticated; retries and a dead letter queue are missing; bulk upload is sequential.

nodes.label: JWT Authentication & Authorization
nodes.rationale: Single login endpoint for all roles (ADMIN, RECRUITER) rather than per-role login logic, because both are User records and role only determines authorization. JWT is stored in an HttpOnly cookie with 1hr expiry and carries only userId/role/companyId to limit XSS exposure and avoid leaking confidential data in the token.

nodes.label: Non-Confidential Response DTOs
nodes.rationale: CompanyRegistrationResponse, LoginResponse, UserResponse and JobResponse exist so JPA entities are never serialized directly and password/hash fields cannot leak through an API boundary.

nodes.label: Frontend API Layer
nodes.rationale: Centralizes auth.getMe/logout/updateMe, assessment, interview and user endpoints and keeps User, Company and JobsMetrics TypeScript interfaces aligned with the backend response DTOs so drift surfaces at compile time.

nodes.label: Frontend AuthContext
nodes.rationale: Loads the user on initial mount via GET /auth/me rather than trusting a cached client value, which is required because the JWT lives in an HttpOnly cookie the JS cannot read.

nodes.label: DTO Boundary Rules
nodes.rationale: Request DTOs carry only client-controlled information; backend-controlled fields are assigned by the service. companyId is deliberately omitted from recruiter/job creation requests when it can be derived from authentication, so there is no field to forge.

nodes.label: MapStruct Mapping with Ignored Backend Fields
nodes.norm_label: mapstruct mapping with ignored backend fields
nodes.rationale: MapStruct request mappings ignore id, role, company, password, createdAt, updatedAt, emailVerified and phoneNumberVerified so an incoming DTO cannot silently overwrite backend-owned state. Password encoding is kept in the service, not the mapper, so BCrypt is never skipped by a mapping path.

nodes.label: Password Handling Rules
nodes.rationale: Passwords are always BCrypt encoded, never logged, never placed in a JWT and never exposed in response DTOs, because a JWT is readable by anyone holding it and logs are a common exfiltration path.

nodes.label: JWT Claim Policy
nodes.rationale: Only sub, userId, role, companyId, iat and exp are allowed; password, password hash, phone number, company detail, candidate and resume information are excluded because a JWT identifies the user but does not authorize anything on its own - database queries and backend checks enforce actual ownership.

nodes.label: Resume Upload Flow
nodes.rationale: Multipart upload at /api/recruiter/candidates/upload persists metadata in PostgreSQL and the PDF on disk, then the AI service extracts, chunks with section inference, extracts a profile with an LLM, embeds and stores in Qdrant.

nodes.label: Java-Side Flow Orchestration (10 steps)
nodes.rationale: Java owns the orchestration sequence (save file, Tika extract, create Resume and Candidate, then call parse/score/summarize and persist each result), with the frontend polling or using WebSocket for completion, because the AI calls are long-running and must not block the upload response.

nodes.label: PythonAiClient (planned Java WebClient client)
nodes.rationale: A single @Service wrapping WebClient exposing scoreCandidate, generateSummary and rankCandidates, so all Java-to-Python HTTP concerns (timeout, api-key, retries) live in one place.

nodes.label: Planned Weighted Scoring Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Configurable weights skills_match 0.40, experience_match 0.25, education_match 0.15, job_relevance 0.20; weights are externalized so the mix can be tuned per deployment without changing the scoring code.

nodes.label: Resume Screening & Ranking End-to-End Flow
nodes.rationale: Resume Upload -> Extract Details -> Create Candidate -> AI Scoring (Python) -> RAG Summary -> Ranking, with React calling Spring Boot and Spring Boot calling the Python AI service, so the Java backend stays the single owner of relational data and auth.

nodes.label: Missing Resumes Page
nodes.rationale: Known broken link: the sidebar exposes /resumes but no route or component exists, so resume upload has no UI entry point even though the backend upload endpoints are implemented.

nodes.label: Java-Python Score Candidate API Contract
nodes.rationale: The request bundles the whole job (including jdEmbedding and weighted required/preferred skills) and the whole resume (including resumeEmbedding) so the Python service can score statelessly without reading the Java database.

nodes.label: Key Technical Decisions (Tika, Ollama, pgvector, async)
nodes.norm_label: key technical decisions (tika, ollama, pgvector, async)
nodes.rationale: Apache Tika does the initial Java-side extract while Python does structured parsing; embeddings use Ollama nomic-embed-text from both sides; vector search reuses the already-configured pgvector rather than adding a store; @Async + CompletableFuture keeps Python calls off the request thread; retries plus a dead letter queue handle failed analyses; job and resume embeddings are cached after first generation.

nodes.label: RecruitAI Frontend App Shell
nodes.rationale: Single-root Vite SPA entry mounting /src/main.tsx as an ES module; Inter and Plus Jakarta Sans are preconnected and loaded from Google Fonts to support the glassmorphic typography tokens.

nodes.label: AI Resume Screening Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Text extraction, normalization, embedding generation and vector storage on the resume side are compared to the job embedding by semantic similarity to produce a matching score, with an LLM explanation layered on top so the score is defensible, not opaque.

nodes.label: End-to-End Recruitment Workflow
nodes.rationale: Company registration and verification, then admin creates recruiters, recruiter creates jobs and uploads resumes, then parse, embed, compare, score, explain, rank, shortlist, assess, interview and AI interview analysis to final evaluation.

nodes.label: Candidate Pipeline Kanban Board
nodes.rationale: Drag-and-drop over 8 status columns with real-time status updates, implemented with @dnd-kit, so recruiters move candidates through the recruitment workflow directly rather than editing a status field in a form.

nodes.label: Glassmorphic Design System
nodes.rationale: A single set of design tokens (pastel palette, 8/16/24px backdrop blur, 10-40px radii, diffuse-only shadows, semi-transparent borders) is defined once as CSS variables so every component reads from the same source and light/dark stay consistent. Dark mode re-bases glass on rgba(20,18,35,opacity) with adjusted blur and border opacity rather than inverting colors, because frosted surfaces lose definition on dark backgrounds.

nodes.label: Python AI Service Boundary
nodes.rationale: AI lives in Python and communicates over HTTP REST returning JSON, but Java Spring Boot explicitly remains the main backend: 'Do not move the entire application to Python.' This keeps auth, tenancy and relational data in one trusted service.

nodes.label: AI-Powered Recruitment Platform Overview
nodes.rationale: Combines traditional recruitment workflow management with resume parsing, semantic job-resume matching, embeddings, LLM analysis, RAG, scoring, ranking, assessments, coding evaluation and interview analysis in one platform.

nodes.label: Job.description as TEXT instead of @Lob
nodes.rationale: Changed from @Lob to @Column(columnDefinition="TEXT") to fix JpaSystemException 'Unable to access LOB stream'. PostgreSQL TEXT needs no LOB handling, so lazy-loading description in getAllJobsForAdmin() no longer hits 'Large Objects may not be used in auto-commit mode'. @Transactional was also switched to Spring's annotation because it supports readOnly.

nodes.label: Company Terminology Rule
nodes.rationale: 'Company' is mandated and 'Organization' is forbidden across database, entity and business vocabulary so naming stays searchable and mapping/repository method names line up with entity properties.

nodes.label: Minimal Change / No Unnecessary Abstraction Policy
nodes.norm_label: minimal change / no unnecessary abstraction policy
nodes.rationale: Inspect before writing, reuse existing services, do not rewrite unrelated code and preserve existing API contracts, so incremental AI-assisted edits cannot quietly redesign the project or break consumers.
